surfaces.part: lake terrain tile (dark teal water with sand edge on right)

answer.evidence: The 16x16 tile is a full-bleed terrain autotile: dark teal water fills rows 0-15 across columns, with a sand strip on the right edge and lighter teal shoreline pixels at the left and right edges. The column scan shows one uniform run per column (rows 0-15). There is no standing object, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. It is a flat ground/water tile, so there is no front face and no top surface to measure.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a tiny dark teal block with a thin sandy edge, far smaller than a 4x3-tile ground patch, so it does not read as the same kind as the grass and paving references. Its body is mostly one flat teal fill with only a narrow lighter strip, which is about 3 lightness steps against roughly 5 on the references. The measured near-flat coverage is 42% against 0% on both references, which agrees with what I see. The 10 visible tones per tile look inflated by the edge strip and do not make up for the lack of grain, tufts or per-stone shading. Dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so there is no sticker outline, but the piece has no real outline structure either. Next to the references it looks flatter and thinner, and it should be redrawn as a full 4x3 sand patch with dotted grain and several sand tones.
